newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Dhaka bourse to switch to automated trading.
newsitem.headline: Dhaka bourse to switch to automated trading.

text.p: The Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE) announced on Friday that it would switch to automated trading from the existing open outcry method in six months.
"We are working on switching to the most modern remote trading system. We are preparing for the 21st century," DSE Chairman Imtiyaz Husain told a news conference.
Husain said the DSE authorities had already chosen the software supplier, and the installation was expected to be completed in the next six months.
He said a DSE delegation would soon visit India where a similar "remote trading" system was in operation.
"The market is growing very fast and it will grow 10 times in the next one-and-half years. Automation is an urgent need," Husain said.
DSE members said they will not have to go to the floor and can trade from their offices once the automation was complete.
The DSE all-share price index stood at 3,298 on November 20 from 775.65 at the end of January this year.
"Automation would also help to offset the growing trade in the kerb market," said Khurshid Alam, a former DSE chairman.

Trading on the DSE was suspended on Thursday following clashes between kerb market traders, protesting against alleged "manipulation" of share prices, and police. Friday is counted as weekend in Moslem Bangladesh.

DSE is the only bourse in the capital Dhaka, but the Finance Minister S.A.M.S. Kibria said on Thursday that the government had decided to allow a second exchange in the city. The country's second bourse is in the port city of Chittagong.
Husain said an independent Central Depository System (CDS) was also planned to prevent forgery and manipulation in trading.
He also announced that the membership of DSE would soon be increased to 250 from the existing 195.
"Besides institutionalising the stock exchange, we are also encouraging our members to institutionalise themselves. We are assisting them on corporatisation," Husain said.
